listenings.text: Okay, most embarrassing minute of my life, and it was last week. So we were in history, and I was drawing on the corner of my notebook, obviously not listening. The teacher was explaining something about a treaty. And then she said my name. Just my name, nothing else. So I panicked and I said yes. Yes! And the question was not a yes-or-no question, it was which country signed it first. The whole class turned around. And I froze. I sat there for about five seconds saying absolutely nothing, while thirty people looked at me. She just moved on. Kindest thing anyone has ever done.

Good afternoon. A quick word about yesterday's power cut. The lights went out at twenty past two, in the middle of the afternoon. At that moment, most of you were in class, some were finishing lunch, and a group in the science lab were finishing an experiment, which we are told did not survive. The power came back forty minutes later. What we want to say is thank you. Nobody panicked, nobody ran, everyone waited quietly where they were, and the teachers could count all of you in under five minutes. That is exactly how it should work.
